label: token right after an early h (h at position 0 or 1)
explanation: Fires in the original phase at step 1 or 2 when the previous input was h, i.e. the token right after an h that opened the sequence or came second. The input token at the firing step makes no difference. Activations are strongest at t=1 (sequence starts with h, about 0.95-1.0 of max) and weaker at t=2 (h in position 1, about 0.5-0.7 of max). Step 1 carries about 65% of the activation mass on roughly the same number of activations as step 2. It is essentially silent after an h at later positions (t>=3), on the delimiter, and in the copy phase (42 tiny copy-phase activations). There is a small low-magnitude tail at t=1-2 after other tokens, mainly the digit 2.

issues: None of the claims could be refuted. On the test split the predicate (prev_tok == tok("h")) & (t <= 2) scored precision 1.0, recall 0.978, F1 0.989 and mass recall 0.9997, with 0 false positives.
The t=1 / t=2 split checks out. t==1 alone gives mass recall 0.651 on 16472 predicted steps; t==2 alone gives 0.349 on 16620. Activations at t=1 are about 0.95-1.0 of max and at t=2 about 0.5-0.7.
The claim that it is silent at t>=3 holds: (prev_tok==h)&(t==3) has precision 0.008. The delimiter has 0 activations and the copy phase has 42 tiny ones (dev).

All 753 test-split misses together carry 0.0% of the activation mass. Most are '2 b' at step 1 with activation about 0.00; the rest are scattered tiny activations (0.01-0.11) at t=3 after h or in the copy phase. This is low-magnitude noise, not a real counterexample class.

Minor imprecision: the digit-2 tail is not 'after 2' in general. (prev_tok==2)&(t<=2) has precision 0.017, so the tail is concentrated on step-1 'b' after a leading 2. The higher in_tok=b count (1751 vs about 1150 for other tokens) comes from this near-zero tail, not from a real input-token dependence. This does not affect the label.
